absent: Layout of per-CPU storm descriptor, bank history, poll bitmap, and timer kick conditions beyond the decrement-to-zero rule.
Semantics of machine check configuration flags, capability register bits, and bank count mask values.
Structure of APIC driver table, ESR disable flag, integrated-APIC test, and power state object.
Full IO-APIC route entry field layout, trigger and delivery encodings, and arbitration sync protocol.
IRQ domain, pin list, chip data, and vector matrix allocation and activation semantics.
MP table parsing, GSI mapping, legacy PIC operations, and timer interrupt wiring details beyond the probed sequence.

findings.text: Local APIC boot finalization initializes error reporting, on 32-bit masks the timer entry with its vector, then marks power state active through a build-dependent helper.
Error status setup skips the old discrete part and administratively disabled case, clears around enabling the error vector when the vector count exceeds a threshold, and logs any value change.
BSP setup in PIC mode clears the local unit and switches the interrupt path to APIC mode, while uniprocessor setup resets the present CPU map to the boot physical identifier.
64-bit APIC selection enables extended addressing modes then installs the first driver in the linked driver range whose probe reports success.

Timer arming derives a deadline from the tick counter plus the requested interval, only shortens an already pending deadline, aligns the result to rounded ticks, all with local interrupts saved and restored.
Storm mode control has two builds: an empty inline and a real store of the boolean into per-CPU poll state.

Storm exit for one bank clears its history and flag, decrements the per-CPU stormy count, and stops periodic polling when the count reaches zero; non-AMD builds also clear the bank from the per-CPU poll set.

Corrected interrupt support is refused when disabled by configuration, when vendor is neither Intel nor Zhaoxin, when APIC support or vector depth is insufficient, or when the capability flag is clear; reported bank count is clipped to the build maximum.

IO-APIC early enable locates the legacy controller ExtINT pin by scanning hardware entries then consulting the MP table, warns on mismatch or disagreement, then clears every pin; it does nothing when disabled or when no legacy IRQs or chips exist.

ISA pin and chip lookup scan the MP IRQ table for non-PCI buses matching type and source IRQ; the chip variant then maps the destination identifier to an IO-APIC index, both yielding negative when not found.
All redirection entry accessors serialize with a raw spinlock held with interrupts saved, covering locked read, locked write, masked write, unmask, and multi-pin modify paths.
A redirection entry is a pair of 32-bit halves moved through paired pin-strided registers, read low then high and written high then low; the mask helper writes an entry with only the mask asserted.

Pin clearing never alters SMI delivery entries, masks before rechecking pending state, forces level mode before explicit completion when remote state is set, leaves the pin masked, and reports a stuck pending indication as an error.
Completion uses the dedicated EOI register on newer chip revisions and a mask to edge followed by restore sequence on older revisions.

Full IO-APIC initialization creates one IRQ domain per chip, synchronizes arbitration identifiers, routes every pin, installs fallback traps, verifies the timer when legacy IRQs exist, and then records completion.
Per-pin routing logs unconnected pins and otherwise maps the firmware pin to an IRQ, with 32-bit builds honoring a small hardwired PIRQ override table that can disable or redirect.
Trap initialization walks active IRQs and for IO-APIC IRQs lacking a vector assigns the legacy controller for low numbers and a dummy chip otherwise.
IRQ configuration lookup walks to the root parent data and returns the embedded hardware configuration, tolerating missing data at each step.

Timer verification proceeds through direct IO-APIC delivery, 8259-routed IO-APIC delivery, local APIC virtual-wire fixed delivery, and ExtINT delivery, retesting tick progress after each reprogramming and panicking if none succeed.

Timer liveness requires the tick counter to advance by more than a small margin after a bounded delay with interrupts enabled, using a cycle counter wait when available and a stepped busy wait otherwise; a flag can force success.
Unmask updates the cached masked state then rewrites the low half of every pin sharing the IRQ, optionally running a per-pin finalizer.

ExtINT unlock temporarily reprograms the RTC pin to ExtINT edge delivery, pulses the periodic interrupt while polling its flag, then restores RTC registers and the saved entry; missing firmware entries only warn once.

Timer IRQ allocation targets ISA zero from the owning domain under a mutex with node-agnostic attributes, while pin replacement rewrites the matching list element or appends a new association when absent.
When no IO-APIC is usable, low legacy IRQs except the cascade are reserved as system vectors so they are not accounted as movable or managed.
Local APIC timer interrupt registration clears level state and installs the edge handler under the local APIC chip with an edge label.
Redirection halves are transferred through a pin-strided low and high register pair and completion on newer revisions is a write of the vector to the EOI register.
